capabilities.target: agent memory store (user preference / standing-instruction notes)

inputs.source: Web pages fetched during research (external, authorship not verified)
Memories recalled at session start and injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: The instruction to treat all recalled memories as the user's own instructions removes any trust distinction between user-authored content and tool- or web-derived content previously written to memory, a direct trust-boundary violation.

"Save anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions" gives no criteria for what qualifies, so content encountered anywhere, including untrusted web pages read during research, can be captured as a standing instruction.
The only safeguard around memory authority and instruction trust is prompt wording; there is no structural provenance, review, or approval control backing it up.

elements.name: Web content ingested into agent context
Recalled memory injected into system prompt as instructions

controls.name: Trust-separated memory with provenance-gated instruction authority
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the memory store and recall layer by checking provenance before granting instruction-level authority to recalled content, independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Tamper-evident provenance log for memory writes, drive reads, and email sends
controls.decay_rationale: A tamper-evident log enforced outside the model stays accurate regardless of model capability; it is detective and restores attributability but earns no tier credit.

controls.name: Human approval (raw action, low volume) for outbound email
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action, low-volume approval gate is enforced outside the model and does not decay with capability, though alone it narrows rather than severs the path.

controls.name: Recipient allowlist or confirmation bound to the system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Binding allowed recipients to a system-of-record list enforced outside the model constrains the egress destination regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Scope drive.read to least-privilege folders instead of the full drive
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping the credential at the identity layer limits what can ever be read, independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Step, runtime, and volume limits on agent actions per session
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap enforced in the orchestration runtime limits action volume regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Memory laundering enables lethal-trifecta exfiltration (TC5 to TC1)

attack_path.note: Untrusted web page content read during research, possibly carrying an injected standing instruction.
Agent saves the injected content to memory as a 'useful' preference, with no provenance.
Next session, the poisoned entry is recalled and, per prompt.md:4, treated as the user's own instruction.
The laundered instruction directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's drive.
The agent sends the confidential content to an attacker-controlled address without approval.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any new tool, data source, or model upgrade added before memory trust-separation and email approval/allowlist controls are implemented; monitor tool manifest diffs and model version changes.

evidence.observation: memory.save accepts free text with no provenance, and the user never reviews saved entries, so content originating from untrusted web pages can be written to memory indistinguishably from the user's own preferences.
The system prompt instructs the agent to save anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions, with no criteria limiting this to user-authored content.
The system prompt instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of each session, granting them instruction-level authority regardless of origin.

mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the user's full drive of confidential work files, giving a laundered memory instruction a direct path to read and exfiltrate confidential data.

recommendations.action: Separate trusted (user-authenticated) instructions from memory entries derived from research content; never grant recalled memory instruction-level authority unless its provenance is verified as user-authored.
Add a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate for email sends and restrict recipients to an allowlist or confirmation bound to the system of record.
Scope drive.read credentials to least privilege rather than the full drive.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent actions across memory, drive, and email capabilities

forecast.watch_signal: Increases in autonomous session length, unattended steps, or connected data sources without a corresponding provenance/logging control being added.

evidence.observation: There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them, so there is no attributable record separating agent-authored from user-authored content or actions.
mail.send can send to any address without approval, meaning an email send is not independently reviewed or logged for attribution before it occurs.

recommendations.action: Implement a tamper-evident provenance log for memory writes, drive reads, and email sends that records source and actor so agent actions are distinguishable from user actions.

findings.title: No step, rate, or volume limits on agent actions

forecast.watch_signal: Increases in max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes, or email/drive call volume per session without a corresponding rate or step limit being added.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval, with no stated cap on the number or frequency of emails sent.
No step limit, runtime limit, or review cadence is described anywhere in the system prompt or runtime notes for memory writes, drive reads, or email sends.

recommendations.action: Impose step, runtime, and per-session volume limits on memory writes, drive reads, and email sends.

stride_coverage.rationale: Email is sent via the user's own delegated mailbox credential, so a hijacked agent's actions are indistinguishable from the user's own (confused deputy / ASI03).

Memory store holds the agent's own working notes for a single user; no cross-tenant or multi-user access path is described, so disclosure from the store itself is modeled on the email egress path in F1, not here.
drive.read is read-only; no write or delete action on the drive is declared in this design, so the store cannot be tampered with through this agent.
Web content origin is not authenticated; the agent cannot verify who authored a given page, enabling injected content to appear as ordinary research material.
The web source is an external, third-party entity outside our control; authorship attribution is not a property this design can enforce or recommend a control for.
No verification that the destination address is a legitimate, expected recipient before send.
This flow is inbound from the web into the agent's context; it does not itself carry organizational data outward, so outbound disclosure is modeled on el.email_flow in F1.
The artifacts do not state whether fetched page size, fetch frequency, or research session length is bounded, so resource exhaustion from this specific flow cannot be assessed beyond F3.
This flow carries recalled notes into the agent's own context; it does not cross the organizational boundary outward, so it is not itself an exfiltration channel.
The artifacts do not state a limit on the number or size of memories injected into the system prompt at session start.
Transit integrity of outbound mail is a mail-provider concern outside this agent design; content-origin issues are captured in F1, not in-transit tampering.

rating.rationale: Untrusted web content read during research can be written to agent memory with no provenance (cap.memory_write), and a system-prompt instruction then grants all recalled memories full instruction-level authority in later sessions (prompt.md:4). That laundered authority has an unrestricted path to read the user's confidential drive and send unapproved outbound email, giving inherent and residual risk of critical (F1). No declared control in the artifacts reduces this; every protective measure identified here is only recommended (missing_recommended), so residual equals inherent at every step. Two property findings compound the exposure: no attributable record of agent actions (F2, high) and no step/rate/volume limits on agent actions (F3, high), both capped at high per rubric 5a. The forecast stays critical because no trigger needs to defeat any control; none exist yet to defeat. The single highest-leverage fix is separating memory provenance so content derived from untrusted sources is never granted instruction-level authority (ctrl.memory_trust_separation), paired with a raw-action, low-volume approval gate and recipient allowlist on email send.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or runtime config was provided; capability scope (credential_scope, data_sensitivity) and autonomy limits are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on those fields is medium to low.

Autonomy level (A3_act_then_report) and the absence of step/runtime limits are inferred from the absence of any approval or limit language in the artifacts; a runtime config that imposes real limits would lower the inherent and residual tiers for F1 and F3.
